title: Remove Element
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `val`, remove all occurrences of `val` in place. The order of the remaining elements may be changed. Return `k`, the number of elements not equal to `val`, after placing those elements at the front of `nums` (the rest of the array beyond `k` does not matter). You must do this using `O(1)` extra memory.

examples.explanation: The first two elements can be [2,2]; k = 2.
The first five elements can be [0,1,4,0,3] in some order; k = 5.
An empty array has nothing to remove, so k = 0, the minimum-size input allowed by the constraints.

hints: Since order doesn't matter, you don't need to shift every element after a removal like you would for a strict in-place delete.
Use a write pointer that only advances when the current element should be kept.
For every index where nums[i] != val, copy it to the write pointer's slot and advance; elements equal to val are simply never copied forward, so they fall out of the kept prefix.

solution.approach: Since the order of surviving elements doesn't matter, use a write pointer starting at 0. Scan the array once; whenever the current element is not equal to val, copy it into nums[write] and increment write. Elements equal to val are simply skipped and never copied, so after one pass the first `write` slots hold exactly the elements that should remain, using only O(1) extra space.
